      Office hours scheduler

      Next office hours

        You can book the same time as other students. Booking is how I know you are coming, so book before you show up.

        Below 45% raw on an IA?

        You must attend office hours once a week in Quarter 2. Your raw score is in the notes on PowerSchool, and it converts to a curved score of 78 or below. If you do not attend, you are not eligible for any curves in Q2. See Academic expectations.

        Missed classwork?

        Office hours are required to make it up. If you do not come, it is a zero. See Academic expectations.

        Academic expectations

        ExpectationsGradesFAQ

        Classwork is done in class

        Classwork can only be done during class.

        Missed assessments

        You can make up an assessment during assessment hour every Wednesday from 3:30 to 4:30. If you do not attempt an assessment, it is a zero.

        Missed classwork

        If you miss classwork, you must come to office hours to complete it. If you do not, it is a zero.

        Low Interim Assessment score

        If you scored below 45% raw on your IA, you are required to attend office hours once a week in Quarter 2. Your raw score is in the notes on PowerSchool, and it converts to a curved score of 78 or below. If you do not attend, you are not eligible for any curves in Q2.

        IA reflection, due November 13

        If you scored below 75% raw on your IA (a curved score of 89 or below), you are required to complete the IA reflection by Friday, November 13. It is a Google Form with a section for each skill. Open it from the button on Home, from Review resources, or from Google Classroom, and plan on about an hour.

        Notebook every day

        Bring your notebook to class every day. It is expected to have an up-to-date table of contents.

        No AI in your solutions

        Your work has to be your own thinking. Do not use AI to produce solutions. If you do use it, you must explain the whole solution, fully and in your own words, in a video.

        Uncommon expectations

        From the Uncommon Schools NYC student and family handbook, SY26-27.

        Be on time, every day

        Arrive on time and ready to learn. If you are absent, you or your family should email the school that day. More than 18 absences makes a student chronically absent, which can put promotion at risk.

        Phones and devices stay off and out of sight

        Phones, smartwatches, earbuds and smart glasses must be off and out of sight in the building. Staff can take a device and your family will be contacted. Use only your own school account, never share passwords, and do not install software without permission.

        Academic integrity

        Cheating and other academic integrity violations can lead to discipline. Do not put your own or anyone else's personal information into AI tools.

        Homework is due the same night

        Homework is due the night of the lesson, by 2 am. Scan it and upload it with the Submit button on the assignment. If you truly cannot scan or upload, email Mr. Hooshmand ahead of time at rumi.hooshmand@uncommonnyc.org and hand it to him in person before first period.

        Homework is practice

        Homework builds independent work, self-discipline and time management. Do it yourself.

        Uniform

        Wear the Uncommon uniform at all times: logo shirt tucked in, dark gray bottoms, all-black sneakers or black or brown shoes, and a black or brown belt with pants.

        Respect and routines

        Be respectful, no profanity, and no interrupting. No gum on campus. Do not skip class. Do not bring toys or other personal items unless a teacher asks you to.

        More rules and expectations will be added here.

        See my grades in PowerSchool

        Grades

        The scale

        Grades run from 55 to 100. The lowest passing grade is a C, and you need a cumulative average of at least 70 for the year to pass a course.

        Report cards

        Report cards come out four times a year, at the end of each quarter.

        Honor Roll

        You earn Honor Roll each quarter with all B's or better, and High Honors with straight A's. It goes on your permanent report card.

        Moving up

        Uncommon does not promote students who have not met the standards. In high school, failing one or two core courses means you must attend and pass summer school to move up. Failing three or more means repeating the grade, and a repeated grade means retaking every course.

        Summer school credit recovery

        Summer school runs six weeks. To pass, you must attend at least 90% of class time, complete at least 90% of classwork, homework and assessments, and earn 70% or higher. A high pass replaces the failed grade with a 75, and a pass replaces it with a 70.

        Attendance counts

        More than 18 absences makes a student chronically absent, which can lead to repeating the grade.

        FAQ

        Privacy and terms

        Last updated November 6, 2026

        This is the class website for Mr. Hooshmand's Algebra II classes at Uncommon Leadership Charter High School. It is written in plain language. It does not replace your school's own policies, which always apply.

        Privacy

        Artificial intelligence

        No AI model is used when you use this site. The practice questions in Teach me something and Practice are made by ordinary computer code that runs in your own browser. It picks numbers at random and checks your answers with fixed math rules. Your answers are not sent to an AI model, they are not sent to any server, and they are not used to train any model.

        Mr. Hooshmand designs this site and uses an AI assistant to help write its code. The lessons, notes, videos and corrections are his, and he reviews everything before students see it.

        What this site does not do

        • It has no accounts or logins.
        • It does not ask for your name, email or grades.
        • It has no ads, and it does not track you or sell anything.
        • Your practice answers and scores are not sent anywhere.

        What stays on your device

        The site saves a few small settings in your own browser: your progress in Teach me something, the class password if you enter it, whether you have seen the site tour, and your display choices. Only you can see them. They never leave your device, and clearing your browser data removes them.

        Other services the site uses

        Some parts of this site run on or link to other services. Each one has its own privacy policy and can see standard information like your IP address when you open it.

        • GitHub Pages hosts the site.
        • Google Fonts supplies the typefaces.
        • Google Drive, Docs and Forms hold class files, notes, videos and forms, including homework submission and the IA reflection.
        • YouTube and similar services may play embedded videos.
        • Khan Academy and other websites are linked for extra help.

        Forms

        When you use a form linked from this site, what you type goes to the person who owns the form, which is Mr. Hooshmand, through Google. Only enter what the form asks for. Do not enter passwords or private information about other people.

        Terms

        • Who it is for. This site is for students and families in Mr. Hooshmand's classes. Please use it for learning.
        • Class materials. Packets, notes and similar materials come from Uncommon Schools and are shared for enrolled students only. Do not post, copy or share them outside the class.
        • The class password. The password for Take this class is for students in the class. Please do not share it.
        • Honest work. Follow your school's academic honesty rules. Practice and checking tools are there to help you learn. They are not a substitute for doing the work.
        • Mistakes happen. Practice problems are generated by a program. If an answer looks wrong, tell Mr. Hooshmand and he will fix it. The site is provided as is. It may change or go down without notice.
        • Grades. Progress shown on this site is for practice. It is not your grade.

        Questions

        Email Mr. Hooshmand at rumi.hooshmand@uncommonnyc.org. If these terms and your school's policies ever disagree, your school's policies win.
